summary: background backfill + health-probe telemetry consuming burst credits and triggering rate rejects
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sustained 'rate-limited' responses (HTTP 429) during a scheduled embeddings backfill. This started after enabling a larger autoscale window on their Dedicated pool and coincides with increased background telemetry/health probes from their orchestrator.

Impact: HollowAI's nightly backfill jobs fail intermittently; ~30% of bulk embed batches return 429 and the job churns retries for hours. Customer reported user-facing lag for model-based search updates.

Environment: Dedicated pool (eu-west), tenant ID: hollowai-74, routes: /v1/embeddings (bulk) and /v1/chat (interactive), autoscaler policy: aggressive-burst (scale to 8 GPUs within 90s).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Queue a sustained (200 rps) bulk embedding backfill using their existing API key (shared across services).
2) Ensure orchestrator's heartbeat frequency is default (every 15s) and sidecar healthchecks enabled.
3) Observe burst window over the next 10–30 minutes; watch for 429 spikes on bulk endpoint.

Observed behavior: Intermittent 429s start once autoscaler warms additional nodes; logs show high token accounting for the tenant even though bulk payloads are the only heavy traffic. Health probes and telemetry POSTs from the customer's ingest coordinator are counted against the same burst budget and appear to drain short-window credits.

Expected behavior: Background telemetry and health probes should not push a production bulk backfill into a short-window exhaustion state for interactive or bulk lanes; recommend separation or different priority accounting.

Customer asks: Can Redwood explain why telemetry/health probes appear to exhaust burst credits and provide short-term mitigations and a long-term config for dedicated pools to avoid similar churn?
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 02:03 UTC: Customer opened ticket after seeing repeated 429s during scheduled backfill.
- 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: Support reproduced on a small sim tenant using similar config (shared API key + background heartbeats).
- 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC: Instrumented metric: tenant_burst_credit_balance (eu-west) shows sawtooth depletion matching healthcheck cadence.

Hypothesis: Tenant-level token accounting combined with per-route weight means short-window burst budget is depleted by many small health/telemetry POSTs. Autoscaler warmup increases concurrency (more connections from proxies/sidecars) and health probes multiply; rate-limiter charges appear per-request, not exempting small telemetry endpoints.

Logs & traces (examples):
- request_id: r-q7d9-20260310-04, path: /v1/internal/sidecar/health, status: 200, counted_tokens: 120
- request_id: r-x8f2-20260310-04, path: /v1/embeddings, status: 429, counted_tokens: 4096

Dashboards & links:
- Burst budget graph: https://console.redwood.ai/d/tenants/hollowai-74/burst-credit
- Ingress trace (sample): https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/5644c1

Experiment notes:
- Creating an isolated API key for backfill shifted bulk traffic into a different per-key window and reduced 429s immediately (workaround confirmed).
- Reducing sidecar heartbeat frequency to 60s also reduced sawtooth pattern but is intrusive for customer's orchestration needs.

Related PRs/commits considered: PR 4321 (rate-limiter: add per-path exemption config), draft patch for a priority class routing flag.
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Torres (Support): Acknowledged. I've asked SRE to check tenant_burst_credit_balance and edge proxy connection counts.

2026-03-10 SRE on-call (Elena Kuznetsova): We see a repeated pattern where many short POSTs (health/telemetry) count small token units but multiply across N warmed nodes. This matches the customer's burst dropouts.
2026-03-11 Aisha (Customer): We can't easily change heartbeat frequency; can you recommend a config we can change on Redwood's side?

2026-03-12 Miguel (Support): Short-term: create a dedicated API key for backfill (isolates windows) or request an isolated burst pool. We're proposing a config change to exempt /v1/internal/* paths from token counting for dedicated customers (pending review).
2026-03-13 Engineering (Rajiv Menon): Drafted a conservative opt-in flag (route_priority_exempt) for dedicated customers — needs security review and a small ACL change.
resolution:
Workarounds implemented:
- Customer created a dedicated API key for bulk backfills; immediate reduction in 429s observed.
- Support temporarily advised reducing telemetry sampling rate.

Recommended long-term actions:
1) Configure route isolation: advise customer to route background flushes to a distinct API key and assign to a lower-priority route with separate burst window.
2) For Dedicated customers, we can provision an isolated burst pool (Support/Sales action) to keep large backfills from impacting interactive lanes.
3) Engineering: implement opt-in per-path exemption or a priority_exemption flag for internal telemetry paths for dedicated tenants (SEC review required).

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4321 (internal): implement route_priority_exempt flag — owner: Rajiv Menon — target: 2026-04-02.
- Support to coordinate with Account Exec to propose isolated burst pool add-on to HollowAI.

Current status: Customer backfill stable after key split; ticket will remain open until ENG-4321 Infra change lands or customer adopts isolated burst pool.
final_notes: This ticket highlights common footgun: shared API keys + background/system probes can amplify token accounting in short refill windows when autoscaling increases parallel probes. For dedicated customers doing large backfills, recommend isolated keys, explicit route separation, or an isolated burst pool. ENG and Security review required before automatically exempting any path from accounting.
